issues.description: The Person.birthday attribute has inconsistent types between template, solution code, and tests. In the template repository Person.birthday is declared as java.time.LocalDate, and tests (e.g. PersonServiceTest) call setBirthday(LocalDate.now()). However the solution repository's Person class declares the birthday field as String while its getter and setter use LocalDate. This attribute type mismatch is structural and will cause compilation errors or test failures and will confuse students comparing template, tests, and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the birthday attribute type consistent across template, tests, and solution. Change the solution repository's Person.birthday field from String to java.time.LocalDate and ensure the getter and setter use LocalDate (matching the template and tests). Alternatively, if String is intended, update all tests and usages to work with String dates, but the preferred fix is to use LocalDate to match existing tests and the template.

issues.description: The conceptual attribute 'birthday' is represented as a LocalDate in the template code and tests (and is used as such by PersonService.save), but in the solution repository Person.java the 'birthday' field is declared as a String. This mismatch of the same conceptual entity across artifacts will confuse students: they expect to work with LocalDate (as shown in the problem, template, and tests) but the solution's model uses a different representation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the 'birthday' attribute consistent across all artifacts. Preferably change the solution's Person.java to declare 'private LocalDate birthday;' with matching getter/setter returning LocalDate so it aligns with PersonService and the tests (or, alternatively, change PersonService and tests to use String consistently, but aligning the solution to the template/tests is recommended).
